style_1_icd10.name: Diabetes insipidus
style_1_icd10.chapter: IV. Endocrine, nutritional and metabolic diseases (E00-E89)

style_2_guidelines.guideline_authority: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes (2024) / EASD Consensus

clinical_targets.goal: < 7.0% (53 mmol/mol) for most non-pregnant adults (< 8.0% if history of severe hypoglycemia or limited life expectancy)
< 180 mg/dL (10.0 mmol/L) 1–2 hours after start of meal
LDL-C < 70 mg/dL; < 55 mg/dL if established ASCVD

steps_summary: Step 1: First-Line Therapy: Foundation & Organ Protection
Step 2: Second-Line / Dual Add-On Therapy (HbA1c Above Goal)
Step 3: Third-Line & Injectable Therapy (Severe Hyperglycemia / Target Not Met)

steps.title: First-Line Therapy: Foundation & Organ Protection
steps.rationale: Metformin combined with lifestyle intervention remains foundational. However, if patient has established ASCVD, Heart Failure (HF), or Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD), an SGLT2i or GLP-1 RA should be started regardless of baseline HbA1c.

drug_classes.role: Foundational monotherapy for glycemic control without weight gain or hypoglycemia.
drug_classes.dosing: Start 500 mg once or twice daily with meals; titrate weekly up to 2000–2550 mg/day (or 1000–2000 mg XR once daily with dinner).
drug_classes.pearls: Contraindicated if eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m². Reduce dose by 50% if eGFR 30–44. Check vitamin B12 levels periodically.

drug_classes.role: First-line if patient has Heart Failure (HFrEF/HFpEF), ASCVD, or CKD (eGFR 20–60 or albuminuria).
drug_classes.dosing: Empagliflozin 10–25 mg once daily; Dapagliflozin 10 mg once daily.
drug_classes.pearls: Demonstrated major reductions in cardiovascular death, HF hospitalization, and CKD progression. Advise genital hygiene and adequate hydration.

drug_classes.role: First-line if patient has established ASCVD or high ASCVD risk and weight reduction is a primary goal.
drug_classes.dosing: Semaglutide oral 3 mg -> 7 mg -> 14 mg daily; Liraglutide SC 0.6 -> 1.2 -> 1.8 mg daily.
drug_classes.pearls: Potent HbA1c reduction and weight loss. Avoid in personal/family history of Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma or MEN 2.

steps.title: Second-Line / Dual Add-On Therapy (HbA1c Above Goal)
steps.rationale: Select add-on agent based on key patient comorbidity, need for weight loss, hypoglycemia risk, and cost.

drug_classes.role: Add-on when minimizing hypoglycemia is priority and SGLT2i/GLP-1 RA are contraindicated or not tolerated.
drug_classes.dosing: Sitagliptin 100 mg daily; Vildagliptin 50 mg BID; Linagliptin 5 mg daily (no renal adjustment).
drug_classes.pearls: Weight neutral, well tolerated. Never combine DPP-4i with GLP-1 RA (overlapping mechanism).

drug_classes.role: Cost-effective glycemic lowering when newer agents are unavailable or unaffordable.
drug_classes.dosing: Glimepiride 1–4 mg daily with breakfast; Gliclazide MR 30–120 mg daily.
drug_classes.pearls: Carry risk of hypoglycemia and weight gain. Gliclazide has lower hypoglycemia risk than Glibenclamide.

drug_classes.role: Improves peripheral insulin sensitivity; beneficial in non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (MASH).
drug_classes.pearls: Avoid in Heart Failure (NYHA Class I–IV) due to fluid retention. Monitor bone density in postmenopausal women.

steps.title: Third-Line & Injectable Therapy (Severe Hyperglycemia / Target Not Met)
steps.rationale: If HbA1c remains > 1.5–2.0% above goal despite dual/triple oral therapy, or symptomatic catabolism (weight loss, polyuria, ketosis), initiate injectable therapy.

drug_classes.role: Controls fasting glucose; titrated to reach target morning fasting levels.
drug_classes.dosing: Start 10 units/day or 0.1–0.2 units/kg/day once daily at same time; titrate by 2 units every 3 days until fasting glucose 80–130 mg/dL.
drug_classes.pearls: Combine with Metformin and SGLT2i to minimize required insulin dose and avoid excessive weight gain.

pearls: Contraindicated if eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m². Reduce dose by 50% if eGFR 30–44. Check vitamin B12 levels periodically.
Demonstrated major reductions in cardiovascular death, HF hospitalization, and CKD progression. Advise genital hygiene and adequate hydration.
Potent HbA1c reduction and weight loss. Avoid in personal/family history of Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma or MEN 2.
Weight neutral, well tolerated. Never combine DPP-4i with GLP-1 RA (overlapping mechanism).

special_populations.renal_impairment: Metformin: safe down to eGFR 45; max 1000 mg/day if eGFR 30–44; stop if eGFR < 30. SGLT2i (Dapagliflozin/Empagliflozin): maintain down to dialysis for cardiorenal protection (glycemic effect diminishes below eGFR 45). Linagliptin requires no dose adjustment across all stages of CKD.
special_populations.hepatic_impairment: Avoid Metformin in severe hepatic impairment (lactic acidosis risk). Pioglitazone contraindicated if active liver disease/ALT > 3x ULN.
special_populations.pregnancy_lactation: Insulin is the standard of care during pregnancy. Oral agents are generally discontinued.

style_3_monograph.summary: Diabetes insipidus (DI) causes frequent urination. You become extremely thirsty, so you drink. Then you urinate. This cycle can keep you from sleeping or even make you wet the bed. Your body produces lots of urine that is almost all water. DI is different from diabetes mellitus (DM), which involves insulin problems and high blood sugar. The symptoms can be similar. However, DI is related to how your kidneys handle fluids. It's much less common than DM. Urine and blood tests can show which one you have. Usually, DI is caused by a problem with your pituitary gland or your kidneys. Treatment depends on the cause of the problem. Medicines can often help. NIH: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases
style_3_monograph.treatment: Consult healthcare provider for individualized management.
